dedupe_keys.name: dlr highway traffic dlr ht and urban traffic dlr ut trajectory datasets braunschweig

description: The German Aerospace Center (DLR) publishes two trajectory datasets recorded in Braunschweig, Germany. DLR Highway Traffic (DLR HT) comes from the Test Bed Lower Saxony on a motorway, and DLR Urban Traffic (DLR UT) from the Application Platform Intelligent Mobility (AIM) research intersection. Both contain trajectories of traffic participants indexed by object and timestamp with position, speed, acceleration, dimensions and class, together with local weather (wind, sunlight, precipitation, visibility) and road surface data (surface temperature, water layer thickness); the urban set adds the states of all 30 traffic lights and air quality measurements and holds 32,296 trajectories of motorised and vulnerable road users. Metadata give traffic volumes extracted from the trajectories and OpenSCENARIO files that replay them. Coverage is a single motorway section and a single intersection in one city. The data are available to download from Zenodo with PDF documentation (versions 1.2.0 of HT, February 2026, and 1.3.1 of UT, June 2026); the data.europa.eu record lists a closed, non-standard licence, so users should read the terms. Caveats: two short sites cannot represent a network. The trajectories support calibration of microscopic traffic models, weather-dependent driving behaviour studies and scenario-based testing of automated vehicles. They complement the SUMO traffic simulator.
